title: Getting started with FESDIA for steady and dynamic simulation
text: Tne FESDIA package contains functions generate diagenetic profiles, describing cycles C, N, O2, Fe, S P. based OMEXDIA model (Soetaert et al., 1996a, b), extended P, S, Fe dynamics. model describes seventeen state variables, 100 layers: 2 fractions organic carbon (FDET,SDET): fast slow decaying, solid substance. Oxygen (O2), dissolved substance. Nitrate (NO3), dissolved substance. Nitrite (NO2), dissolved substance. Ammonia (NH3), dissolved substance. Dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), dissolved substance Iron 2+ (Fe), dissolved substance Sulphide (H2S), dissolved substance Methane (CH4), dissolved substance Phosphate (PO4), dissolved substance Alkalinity (ALK), dissolved substance Iron hydroxides (FeOH3), solid substance Iron-bound P (FeP), P bound iron oxides, solid substance Ca-bound P (CaP), apatite, solid substance Adsorbed P (Pads), solid substance Time expressed days, space expressed centimeters. Concentrations liquids solids expressed [nmol/cm3 liquid] [nmol/cm3 solid] respectively (Note: [mmol/m3 liquid] [mmol/m3 solid]). Compared OMEXDIA model, FESDIA includes following additions: simple phosphorus, iron sulphur dynamics long-distance H2S CH4 oxidation, e.g. cable bacteria worms associated chemosynthetic bacteria allowing boundary conditions water overlying sediment exposure air. external conditions set either time-variable forcings constant parameters bottom water conditions either imposed dynamically modeled possibility include sediment perturbation events vertical profiles porosity, irrigation, bioturbation either set parameters inputted data. model implemented fortran (speed) linked R (flexibility).
code: require(FESDIA)

title: Getting started with FESDIA for steady and dynamic simulation
text: FESDIA package contains functions generate (time series ) 1-D diagenetic profiles. can either run dynamic mode, steady-state solution can estimated. contains several utility functions, e.g. help extracting information model output, estimate mass budgets. contains functions perturb sediment properties, e.g. mimicking resuspension deposition events. main functions allow solve model steady state (FESDIAsolve), run dynamically (FESDIAdyna), add perturbations (FESDIAperturb) dynamic simulations (discussed another vignette)..

title: Getting started with FESDIA for steady and dynamic simulation
text: Function FESDIAsolve finds steady-state solution FESDIA model. arguments : parms list subset FESDIA parameters (see appendix mean default values). unspecified, default parameters used. gridtype default assumes cartesian grid (gridtype = 1), can 1D cylindrical (gridtype = 2) spherical (gridtype = 3). irregular grid can seleceted specifying surface areas interface argument surface. cartesian grid surface area remains constant. vertical profiles can imposed vector : porosity, bioturbation irrigation, surface (surface areas box interfaces) diffusionfactor (multiplication factor estimate effective sediment diffusion based molecular diffusion). dynamicbottomwater, set TRUE also explicitly model bottom water concentrations. ratefac multiplication factor, multiplied biogeochemical rates. included consistency FESDIAdyna.
code: args(FESDIAsolve) function (parms = list(), yini = NULL, gridtype = 1, Grid = NULL,      porosity = NULL, bioturbation = NULL, irrigation = NULL,      surface = NULL, diffusionfactor = NULL, dynamicbottomwater = FALSE,      ratefactor = NULL, calcpH = FALSE, verbose = FALSE, method = NULL,      times = c(0, 1e+06), ...)  NULL

title: Getting started with FESDIA for steady and dynamic simulation
text: Function FESDIAdyna runs FESDIA model specific time interval produces output requested times. arguments : functions run model dynamically also allow several external conditions either constants vary time. Thus, can set parameter forcing function. conditions : flux carbon, CaP FeP (Cflux, CaPflux, FeOH3flux), forcings CfluxForc, CaPfluxForc, FeOH3fluxForc), bottom water concentrations (O2bw, NO2bw, NO3bw, NH3bw, H2Sbw, PO4bw, DICbw, ALKbw), forcings O2bwForc, NO3bwForc, NO2bwForc, NH3bwForc, ODUbwForc, PO4bwForc, DICbwForc, ALKbwForc) sedimentation, bioturbation bio-irrigation rates (w, biot, irr), (wForc, biotForc, irrForc) decay rates organic matter (rFast, rSlow) fraction fast organic matter present flux (pFast), forcings (rFastForc, rSlowForc, pFastForc) microphytobenthos production rate (MPBprod), (MPBprodForc) air-sea exchange rate exposed air (gasflux), (gasfluxForc) height overlying water (Hwater), (HwaterForc), used dynamicbottomwater TRUE. ratefac (time series constant) multiplication factor, multiplied biogeochemical rates. can used impose temperature dependency. forcing functions either prescribed list either contains data series (list (data = …)) list specifies periodic signal, defined amplitude (amp), period, phase, coefficient defines strength periodic signal (power) minimum value (min) : default settings : list(amp = 0, period = 365, phase = 0, pow = 1, min = 0). mean value sine function given corresponding parameter. instance, C flux, seasonal signal defined : max(min,Cflux*(1+(amp*sin((times−phase)/period*2*pi))pow)max(min, Cflux*(1 + (amp*sin((times-phase)/period*2*pi))^pow).

title: Delving deeper with event-driven early diagenesis with FESDIA
text: Tne FESDIA package contains functions generate diagenetic profiles, describing cycles C, N, O2, Fe, S P. based OMEXDIA model (Soetaert et al., 1996a, b), extended P, S, Fe dynamics. model describes seventeen state variables, 100 layers: 2 fractions organic carbon (FDET,SDET): fast slow decaying, solid substance. Oxygen (O2), dissolved substance. Nitrate (NO3), dissolved substance. Nitrite (NO2), dissolved substance. Ammonia (NH3), dissolved substance. Dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), dissolved substance Iron 2+ (Fe), dissolved substance Sulphide (H2S), dissolved substance Methane (CH4), dissolved substance Phosphate (PO4), dissolved substance Alkalinity (ALK), dissolved substance Iron hydroxides (FeOH3), solid substance Iron-bound P (FeP), P bound iron oxides, solid substance Ca-bound P (CaP), apatite, solid substance Adsorbed P (Pads), solid substance Time expressed days, space expressed centimeters. Concentrations liquids solids expressed [nmol/cm3 liquid] [nmol/cm3 solid] respectively (Note: [mmol/m3 liquid] [mmol/m3 solid]). Compared OMEXDIA model, FESDIA includes following additions: simple phosphorus, iron sulphur dynamics long-distance H2S CH4 oxidation, e.g. cable bacteria worms associated chemosynthetic bacteria allowing boundary conditions water overlying sediment exposure air. external conditions set either time-variable forcings constant parameters bottom water conditions either imposed dynamically modeled possibility include sediment perturbation events vertical profiles porosity, irrigation, bioturbation either set parameters inputted data. model implemented fortran (speed) linked R (flexibility).

text: Function FESDIAperturb runs FESDIA model specific time interval adding perturbations requested times. arguments : functions run model dynamically also allow several external conditions either constants vary time. Thus, can set parameter forcing function. conditions : flux carbon, CaP FeP (Cflux, CaPflux, FeOH3flux), forcings CfluxForc, CaPfluxForc, FeOH3fluxForc), bottom water concentrations (O2bw, NO2bw, NO3bw, NH3bw, H2Sbw, PO4bw, DICbw, ALKbw), forcings O2bwForc, NO3bwForc, NO2bwForc, NH3bwForc, ODUbwForc, PO4bwForc, DICbwForc, ALKbwForc) sedimentation, bioturbation bio-irrigation rates (w, biot, irr), (wForc, biotForc, irrForc) decay rates organic matter (rFast, rSlow) fraction fast organic matter present flux (pFast), forcings (rFastForc, rSlowForc, pFastForc) microphytobenthos production rate (MPBprod), (MPBprodForc) air-sea exchange rate exposed air (gasflux), (gasfluxForc) height overlying water (Hwater), (HwaterForc), used dynamicbottomwater TRUE. ratefac (time series constant) multiplication factor, multiplied biogeochemical rates. can used impose temperature dependency. forcing functions either prescribed list either contains data series (list (data = …)) list specifies periodic signal, defined amplitude (amp), period, phase, coefficient defines strength periodic signal (power) minimum value (min) : default settings : list(amp = 0, period = 365, phase = 0, pow = 1, min = 0). mean value sine function given corresponding parameter. instance, C flux, seasonal signal defined : max(min,Cflux*(1+(amp*sin((times−phase)/period*2*pi))pow)max(min, Cflux*(1 + (amp*sin((times-phase)/period*2*pi))^pow). Three types perturbations possible (argument perturbType): mixing straightens profiles certain depth erosion removes part surficial sediment deposition adds sediment top. perturbations implemented events, need input perturbation times (perturbTimes), depth (perturbDepth). deposition events, factor increase/decrease solid fraction concentration can also inputted (concfac).

code: # ============================= # Plotting dynamic output # =============================    out <- FESDIAdyna(CfluxForc = list(amp = 1))   image2D(out, which = 1:9)      image2D(out, which = "O2", ylim = c(5, 0), mfrow = c(1,2))   matplot1D(out, which = 3, col = "grey", ylim = c(5,0), mfrow = NULL)    O2mean <- FESDIA1D(out, "O2")   head(O2mean) #>            x       por       O2 #> 1 0.00498923 0.8934027 297.6858 #> 2 0.01530360 0.8801069 292.8746 #> 3 0.02631242 0.8664113 287.7195 #> 4 0.03806243 0.8523376 282.2069 #> 5 0.05060354 0.8379122 276.3249 #> 6 0.06398901 0.8231666 270.0640   lines(O2mean$O2, O2mean$x)         # The same but more elaborate   O2 <- subset(out, which = "O2")   image2D(O2, x = out[,"time"], y = FESDIAdepth(out), ylim = c(10,0))  # ============================= # Plotting steady-state output # =============================    std <- FESDIAsolve()   plot(std, which = c("TOC", "O2"))
